dedupe_keys.name: uncertainty quantification for seismic collapse fragilities using sequential bayesian experimental design

description: Maha Kenawy and Aman Karki at Oklahoma State University published Python scripts for sequential Bayesian experimental design to estimate seismic structural performance and collapse fragility. The accompanying simulation data provide benchmark coverage of nonlinear time-history analyses of a twelve-storey reinforced-concrete moment frame at multiple shaking intensities. The method selects informative ground-motion records and seeks to reduce fragility-estimation bias within a fixed simulation budget. Its outputs include structural performance quantities at individual intensity levels and an estimated collapse fragility function. DesignSafe provides public repository access at no stated charge under Creative Commons Attribution; the licence version is unspecified. This is a documented building benchmark, with no geographic transferability claim. Software dependencies, execution and predictive accuracy remain unverified. The accompanying reference simulations support comparisons with other sampling methods. The related DesignSafe Data Depot record describes the repository.
